card.name: Punctuation inside citations and reference lists
card.fires_on: Periods, commas, colons and spaces at breaks in bibliographic references, such as after a journal page range, author list, or scripture-style citation number. Also fires on some sentence-ending periods in web text.

modes.label: Reference list breaks
modes.description: The period or comma that ends a citation entry or separates authors and years.
modes.example: bacteria in throat commensal flora. Int J Antimicrob Agents. 2005;25:68–74<<. >>- Stratchounski LS, And

modes.label: Verse or chapter numbers
modes.description: The period inside a scripture-style citation like Mbh.12.206.
modes.example: Dasarathi Rama. The following passage mentions about a terrible drought that occurred during the life of Viswamitra. Mbh.12<<.>>206:- Towards the end

modes.label: Ordinary sentence ends
modes.description: A period closing a plain web-text sentence before the next one.
modes.example: You can purchase commercially bottled water<<.>> Make sure you check the expiration date.

card.writes: It pushes up words like officials and government and pushes down odd fragments, which suggests a weak link to source or authority text.
card.plain: It marks the punctuation between entries in reference lists and citations.
